title: Bialgebra tangent functionals, contraction and invariant derivations
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $C$ a commutative unital $k$-algebra with a $k$-bialgebra structure: the unital algebra maps $\Delta:C\to C\otimes_k C$ and $\varepsilon:C\to k$ satisfy coassociativity and the two counit identities, using the canonical tensor associativity and unit identifications [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Define the subspace $L\subseteq\operatorname{Hom}_k(C,k)$ of tangent functionals by $x(ab)=\varepsilon(a)x(b)+\varepsilon(b)x(a)$ for all $a,b\in C$. For every $k$-linear functional $x:C\to k$, define its contraction $D_x=(1_C\otimes x)\Delta:C\to C$, followed by $C\otimes_k k\simeq C$. For a $k$-linear derivation $D:C\to C$, meaning $D(ab)=aD(b)+D(a)b$, define left invariance to be the equation $\Delta D=(1_C\otimes D)\Delta$. These are definitions; they assert neither that every contraction is a derivation nor any identification or closure theorem.
